messages:
ravi: quick heads-up — bringing up Gemma-6B converted from Mistral for int8 experiments. did a straight weight-convert + per-channel symmetric 8-bit (outlier_clip=2.5) and the summarization suite (LargeSumm) shows a big regression :confused:. rouge-l down ~6, inferred ppl up ~12%

mira: ouch. which step do you think caused it — tokenization, rotary, or quant scale?

ravi: initial bisect points at two candidates: (1) rotary scaling mismatch during conversion (Mistral export had headwise_scale, our Gemma loader applied global_scale), (2) tokenizer normalization difference — we noticed a handful of non-printing/soft-hyphen tokens mapped differently after conversion.

kai: can you paste the exact eval diff and the minimal repro prompt? also paste the quant config.

ravi: eval snippet: 
```
Model: gemma6b-conv-int8
Bench: LargeSumm (1500 cases)
ROUGE-L: baseline fp16=42.7 -> int8=36.4
Perplexity(on proxy set): fp16=11.2 -> int8=12.5
Top failures: truncation in bullet lists, hallucinated extra sentence in news summaries
```
Quant config: `bits=8, per_channel=true, symmetric=true, outlier_clip=2.5, zero_point=0`

julia: interesting — the hallucination pattern could be rotary-related (phase drift). can you run a short A/B where you force the loader to use headwise_scale vs global_scale? also try re-tokenizing a failing example with NFKC vs NFKD.

ravi: running quick A/B now. kicked off two jobs: `conv-loaders/headwise-scale` and `conv-loaders/global-scale` (30-real-case smoke). ops-bot will post results.

ops-bot: benchmark job completed (id: run-1934). summary: headwise_scale A: ROUGE-L median 41.9 (close to fp16), global_scale B: ROUGE-L median 36.6. token-normalization patch (NFKC) improved a few failure cases but did not recover the full gap.

mira: that pretty strongly implicates rotary scaling. do we know why the converter dropped headwise params? maybe mismatch in metainfo mapping (old field `rotary_scale_per_head` -> new `rotary_scale`).

kai: I'll open a tiny script to diff converter metadata and weight shapes. if converter stripped per-head multiplier broadcast to [heads, dim] -> collapsed to [dim] that's an immediate bug.

julia: if true we should hotfix converter and re-run int8 packer — rotary headwise vs global will change activation distributions, which interacts badly with symmetric per-channel quantization. also consider a calibration pass with EMA clipping instead of fixed 2.5.

ravi: next steps I have: 1) patch converter to preserve headwise_scale, 2) re-quantize with headwise-aware scaler and try outlier_clip=3.5 + ema calibration, 3) run same 1500-case LargeSumm. i'll post a short repro script and minimal failing examples in the thread.

mira: thanks — please include a tiny log of the token ids around the soft-hyphen cases so we can audit tokenizer mapping. if converter didn't touch tokenizer files we can rule out that axis.

ravi: will do. cc @julia for review on converter PR once I have a fix. :thumbsup:
